nodes.name: Webhook: Order
nodes.notes: POST /webhook/orders/incoming, signed with HMAC-SHA256 over "timestamp.rawBody". rawBody is on so the signature is checked against the exact bytes the sender signed.

nodes.name: CONFIG
nodes.notes: THE ONLY NODE YOU NEED TO EDIT. Signing secret, header names, service URLs. See the Read Me First note and the README.

nodes.name: Schedule: Reconcile
nodes.notes: Runs the reconcile job every 15 minutes (edit the interval here). Does nothing unless CONFIG.RECONCILE_ENABLED is true.

nodes.name: Webhook: Reconcile
nodes.notes: POST /webhook/orders/reconcile with header x-reconcile-token: runs the reconcile job now and replies with a summary. Off (403) unless CONFIG.RECONCILE_ENABLED is true.

nodes.name: Webhook: Redrive
nodes.notes: POST /webhook/orders/redrive {order_id} with header x-reconcile-token. Used by the reconcile job (one call per stuck order); also fine to call by hand. Same switch and token as the reconcile job.

parameters.jsCode: return [{ json: { _source: 'reconcile', _via: 'schedule' } }];

nodes.name: Mark Reconcile (schedule)
nodes.notes: Tags the run so it takes the reconcile path after CONFIG.

parameters.jsCode: return [{ json: { ...$input.first().json, _source: 'reconcile', _via: 'api' } }];

nodes.name: Mark Reconcile (api)
nodes.notes: Tags the run so it takes the reconcile path after CONFIG.

parameters.jsCode: return [{ json: { ...$input.first().json, _source: 'redrive', _via: 'api' } }];

nodes.name: Mark Redrive
nodes.notes: Tags the run so it takes the redrive path after CONFIG.

nodes.name: Is Reconcile?
nodes.notes: Order requests, reconcile runs and redrive calls share one CONFIG node; this sends each down its own path.

nodes.name: Reconcile Plan
nodes.notes: Off by default. When on: CONFIG is checked (a scheduled run that cannot start alerts ops), and an API call needs the right x-reconcile-token.

nodes.name: List Stale Received
nodes.notes: GET /events?status=received&older_than_seconds=N&limit=M (pending_manual: status&limit only) -> 200 {events:[record,...]}, oldest first. These were accepted but never finished.

nodes.name: List Pending Manual
nodes.notes: Same list call without an age limit for pending_manual: orders that need a human. They are only reported, never re-run.

nodes.name: Reconcile Triage
nodes.notes: Filters what the store returned (status and age are re-checked here), caps the batch, and decides what to re-run: only stuck "received" orders, and only when RECONCILE_ACTION is "redrive" and both lists could be read. pending_manual orders are never re-run.

parameters.jsCode: return $('Reconcile Triage').first().json.redrive_ids.map((id) => ({ json: { order_id: id } }));

nodes.name: Split Redrive
nodes.notes: One item per stuck order.

nodes.name: Call Redrive
nodes.notes: Calls this workflow's own redrive webhook once per stuck order. Each order is then claimed atomically in the event store, acknowledged, and run through the normal fulfilment path in its own execution.

nodes.name: Redrive Results
nodes.notes: Counts per order: started (claimed and acknowledged), not_claimed (finished or taken by someone else meanwhile), failed (the redrive call itself failed).

nodes.name: Reconcile Report
nodes.notes: The summary for the caller, and one Slack message when something needs attention: stuck orders (or what was re-run), orders waiting for a person, or a problem listing them. Nothing to report = no message.

nodes.name: Send Reconcile Alert
nodes.notes: Slack-compatible incoming webhook. A failed alert is ignored on purpose.

nodes.name: Respond Reconcile
nodes.notes: Replies to the API caller with the summary. A scheduled run has no caller, so this node does nothing there.

nodes.name: Redrive Check
nodes.notes: Same switch and token as the reconcile job. Only an order_id is accepted: the order itself always comes from the event store, never from the caller.

nodes.name: Reclaim For Redrive
nodes.notes: The same atomic claim a late sender retry uses: only an event that is STILL "received" and older than RECONCILE_STALE_SECONDS can be taken (200 claimed:true + the stored record), otherwise 409. This is what stops a double run.

nodes.name: Redrive Verdict
nodes.notes: Claimed -> go. Not "received" any more, or not old enough -> not_claimed (nothing runs). A claimed record without a usable order -> 422 (it stays "received", so the next reconcile reports it again).

nodes.name: Respond Redrive
nodes.notes: Replies at once; the order then runs through the normal fulfilment path with nobody waiting.

nodes.name: Is Redrive Item?
nodes.notes: Order Mapping is also run for a re-driven order, only to read your notices settings (customer templates and ops alerts). The sender payload is not available, so the mapping itself is not used.

nodes.name: Redrive Notices
nodes.notes: Uses the same checked notices settings as a normal order. If they are broken now, the order still runs, customer notices are skipped and ops is told.

nodes.name: Order In Flight
nodes.notes: The one place the fulfilment steps read the order and notices from, so a normal order and a re-driven one use exactly the same nodes.

nodes.name: Prepare Verification
nodes.notes: Reads the exact raw bytes of the request body, finds the signature (and timestamp) the way your sender sends them (CONFIG.SIGNATURE_SCHEME: generic, stripe, github or shopify) and builds the exact string that was signed.

nodes.name: Signature (HMAC)
nodes.notes: Computes HMAC-SHA256 with your signing secret. (A Code node cannot use `crypto` in current n8n; the original did, which is why it returned nothing.)

nodes.name: Check Request
nodes.notes: The security gate. Checks CONFIG, then header presence, timestamp window (replay), and the signature (constant-time compare), then parses the JSON. A bad signature gets a generic 401; the specific reason goes only to the security log. Nothing from the payload is interpreted before this passes.

nodes.name: Respond Early
nodes.notes: Replies to requests that stop early: 400, 401, 409, 500, 503, and duplicates (200).

nodes.name: Order Mapping
nodes.notes: EDIT ME. Sender-specific logic goes here: mapOrder (read the sender's payload format), rules (reject orders), notices (customer templates and ops alert wording). Only edit between the EDIT lines. Validate Order checks the result.

nodes.name: Validate Order
nodes.notes: THE GUARD (do not edit). Checks what Order Mapping produced: the standard order must be valid (ids, amount, currency, items, email), the notices settings must be well formed, a rule rejection gives 422, and an order that needs a human always reaches ops. A broken Order Mapping node gives a clear 500 and nothing is recorded.

nodes.name: Log Security Event?
nodes.notes: Only failed signature checks are logged, and only if SECURITY_LOG_API_URL is set.

nodes.name: Log Security Event
nodes.notes: POST {SECURITY_LOG_API_URL}/security {type, reason, at}. Failure is ignored. Note: unsigned traffic can fill this log; rate-limit upstream.

nodes.name: Payload Hash
nodes.notes: SHA-256 of the raw body. Stored with the event so the same order_id with a DIFFERENT payload can be told apart from a genuine duplicate.

nodes.name: Record Event
nodes.notes: POST /events -> 201 {record} when new, 200 {existing:true, record} when that order_id already exists. ATOMIC create-or-return-existing: this is the idempotency check AND the durable log in one call, so two simultaneous deliveries cannot both pass. Not retried here (a lost reply would look like a duplicate); the sender retries on 503.

nodes.name: Record Verdict
nodes.notes: New -> process. Same order_id, different contents -> 409. Same contents -> 200 duplicate (nothing reprocessed), unless the first delivery was accepted but never finished and is older than RECLAIM_AFTER_SECONDS, in which case it is taken over. Store down -> 503 so the sender retries.

nodes.name: Reclaim Event
nodes.notes: POST /events/{id}/reclaim {stale_after_seconds} -> 200 {claimed:true} only if the event is STILL "received" and older than the lease (atomic); else 409. Rescues an order whose first delivery was acked but whose processing died.

nodes.name: Reclaim Verdict
nodes.notes: Claimed -> process it now. Someone else claimed it -> duplicate. Error -> 503.

nodes.name: Respond Accepted
nodes.notes: The fast ack. The event is already durably recorded, so everything after this node happens with no caller waiting.

nodes.name: Reserve Inventory Transient?

nodes.name: Reserve Inventory (retry)
nodes.notes: The one retry.

nodes.name: Reserve Verdict
nodes.notes: 2xx = reserved. 409 = out of stock -> backordered (normal business outcome). Anything else = the inventory service failed -> pending_manual and ops is paged. The original treated an inventory OUTAGE as "out of stock" and told the customer it was backordered.

nodes.name: Create Order in OMS
nodes.notes: POST /orders {order_id, amount, currency, line_items, customer_email, idempotency_key} -> 2xx created. One retry on transient failure; the order system must de-duplicate on order_id / idempotency_key.

nodes.name: Create Order in OMS Transient?
nodes.notes: Transient failure (no response, 5xx, 408, 429)? One more try. A definite answer (2xx, 4xx) is final.

nodes.name: Create Order in OMS (retry)
nodes.notes: The one retry.

nodes.name: OMS Verdict
nodes.notes: 2xx -> fulfilled. Otherwise pending_manual (after the retry): the order is not lost, it is flagged for a human with the reason. If CONFIG.RELEASE_RESERVATION_ON_OMS_FAILURE allows it (off / rejected = only after a definite 4xx rejection / any), the inventory reservation is released next.

nodes.name: Release Reservation
nodes.notes: POST /release {order_id, idempotency_key, reason} -> 2xx released (404 = nothing was held, also fine). One retry on transient failure. Only called when the order system failed and CONFIG.RELEASE_RESERVATION_ON_OMS_FAILURE allows it.

nodes.name: Release Reservation Transient?
nodes.notes: Transient failure (no response, 5xx, 408, 429)? One more try. A definite answer (2xx, 4xx) is final.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ { order_id: $('Order In Flight').first().json.order.order_id, idempotency_key: 'release:' + $('Order In Flight').first().json.order.order_id, reason: 'oms_create_failed' } }}

nodes.name: Release Reservation (retry)
nodes.notes: The one retry.

nodes.name: Release Verdict
nodes.notes: The order stays pending_manual (a person still has to deal with the order); this only records whether the stock was given back. A failed release is alerted.

parameters.jsCode: return [{ json: { outcome: $input.first().json.outcome } }];

nodes.name: Outcome
nodes.notes: Both paths (out of stock / inventory failed / fulfilled / OMS failed) meet here with one outcome.

nodes.name: Update Event Status
nodes.notes: Writes the final status to the event store: the source of truth a support agent checks. One retry on transient failure; if it still fails ops is alerted.

nodes.name: Update Event Status Transient?
nodes.notes: Transient failure (no response, 5xx, 408, 429)? One more try. A definite answer (2xx, 4xx) is final.

nodes.name: Update Event Status (retry)
nodes.notes: The one retry.

nodes.name: Build Notices
nodes.notes: Builds the customer notices and ops alerts from the Order Mapping notices settings (default: confirmation on fulfilled, backorder notice on backordered, an ops alert on pending_manual). A failed status write is ALWAYS alerted. Built AFTER the status write.

nodes.name: Expand Notifications
nodes.notes: One item per message. Slack or customer notices are skipped if their URLs are blank.

nodes.name: Send Slack Alert
nodes.notes: Slack-compatible incoming webhook. A failed alert is ignored on purpose.

nodes.name: Notify Customer
nodes.notes: POST {NOTIFY_API_URL}/send {to, template, order_id}. Best effort; a failure is ignored.

parameters.content:
## Secured Webhook Order Processor
**Setup (about 10 minutes)**
1. Run the backing services (a reference implementation is included: `node 04-secured-webhook-order-processor-mock-server.js`, port 4800): event store, inventory, order system, customer notifications, security log, Slack stand-in.
2. Open **CONFIG**: **change `WEBHOOK_SIGNING_SECRET`** (the shared secret your sender signs with; the workflow refuses to run with a short one), check the header names, set the service URLs and optional `SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL`.
3. Activate. Senders `POST /webhook/orders/incoming` with headers `x-timestamp` (unix seconds) and `x-signature` = hex HMAC-SHA256 of `timestamp.rawBody`. (Stripe, GitHub or Shopify sender? Set `SIGNATURE_SCHEME` in CONFIG instead.)

**Each order:** verify signature + timestamp -> validate -> record it atomically (this is the duplicate check) -> reply 200 "accepted" -> reserve inventory -> create the order -> save the final status -> notify the customer / alert ops.
